about.title: Indian Wells Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Indian Wells is a small community — about 5,289 residents in Riverside County — and a death here is felt widely. Public records for 2025 list 33 injury collisions and 50 people hurt, with no traffic deaths recorded that year. Most reported crashes cluster along Highway 111, Fred Waring Drive, and Washington Street, with Friday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. showing the highest volume. Wrongful death claims are not limited to the roadway, though. A fall at a resort property, an error in medical care, a defective product, or neglect in a care setting can each give rise to a civil claim when someone's carelessness costs a life. Under California law, the surviving spouse or domestic partner and children hold the first right to bring that claim, and it must generally be filed within two years of the date of death. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm. We connect Indian Wells families with an independent attorney who handles wrongful death cases on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: Indian Wells recorded no traffic deaths in 2025. Can a wrongful death claim still arise here?
items.answer: Yes. Public collision records track only roadway fatalities, and wrongful death claims in Indian Wells frequently stem from other causes — medical negligence, unsafe conditions at hotels or golf properties, defective products, or neglect in care facilities. Residents also travel daily along Highway 111 and Fred Waring Drive into neighboring cities, where a fatal crash would still be handled under the same California law. If someone's carelessness contributed to a death, it is worth asking an attorney whether a claim exists.

items.question: Is a wrongful death case the same as criminal charges against the person responsible?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death action is a civil case brought by the family to recover financial and personal losses, and it proceeds separately from any criminal prosecution the Riverside County District Attorney may pursue. A civil claim can move forward whether or not charges are filed, and its burden of proof is lower. The two processes can run at the same time.

items.question: How long does my family have to act after a death in Indian Wells?
items.answer: California generally allows two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death lawsuit. If a government entity — such as a city, county, or state agency — may share responsibility, a formal claim must be presented much sooner, often within months. Because that shorter window is easy to miss during a period of grief, it helps to speak with an attorney early even if you are not ready to make decisions.
